messages.subject: stanc static is_var in parser
parts:
I am changing the subject since I found it is a different issue. 

The reason is a recent change in generator.hpp:

at line 1203 of generator.hpp , we have a static bool variable is_var, 
which is true at the beginning, but changed to false later.  
It is static, which causes a problem in RStan.  Since there are multiple 
entries into this function (this would not happen for stanc from command line),
in all calls of stanc after the first one, is_var is false, which is the problem 
I have found last (which I thought I should take back).  

I know nothing about the parser.  But could we remove the static?  
Ideally we should avoid something similar happen, I am not sure if we can  
put in some tests. 

--
Jiqiang 





On Mon, Nov 12, 2012 at 9:08 PM, Jiqiang Guo <guo...@gmail.com> wrote:
I need to take bac the following.  I did not notice log_prob is overloaded now. 

So back to the starting point for me. 

--
Jiqiang 


On Mon, Nov 12, 2012 at 8:41 PM, Jiqiang Guo <guo...@gmail.com> wrote:
One reason I found so far is that in the stanc (from command line Stan)-generated cpp code for a model,

I have 

stan::io::reader<var> in__(params_r__,params_i__);
vector<var> y;

while in RStan, it is 

stan::io::read<double> in__(params_r__,params_i__);
vector<double> y;

So I guess I am close to find the reason. 

--
Jiqiang

Sure -- I just removed the static in the latest push.

I should've removed the static when I added the second
half of the generate log prob function and reset it.
What I should've done earlier is declared it const -- I
was just giving boolean constants names to make the code
clearer. With a static const declaration, the compiler would've
slapped my wrist when I tried to reset it.

I'm not sure how to write unit tests for general race
conditions like this -- they can be hard to invoke as
they'll vary based on things like compiler, platform and
debug level. And I don't know how to write multi-threaded
C++ code cross-platform -- one of these days we need to
crack out the Boost thread stuff.

- Bob
